changed_passages.old: \emph{SplitLRP} treats both split-streams as neuron groups in one split network. Each layer carries relevance tensors $R^{(l,+)},R^{(l,-)}$, jointly propagated through the four coupling blocks built from $\Wsig{l}{+},\Wsig{l}{-}$. Propagation starts at the class-specific positive $g$-output $\act{L}{+}$.
changed_passages.new: In the \ac{dc} decomposition, each layer consists of two split-streams, which \emph{SplitLRP} treats as two sets of neurons within a unified model. Accordingly, LRP on the split-pair produces two relevance tensors in each layer, $R^{(l,+)}$ and $R^{(l,-)}$, jointly propagated through the four coupling blocks built from $\Wsig{l}{+},\Wsig{l}{-}$. We propagate relevance from the class-specific positive output $\act{L}{+}$.
changed_passages.source: HM accepted paper p. 24112, SplitLRP implementation details
changed_passages.retention: Preserve coupled split-network semantics and exact output initialization; avoid calling streams separately independent.
